paragraphs.text: An AI agent is software powered by a large language model that can decide what to do next to reach a goal. Instead of only answering a question, it can break a task into steps, call tools such as your CRM, database, calendar or email, check the results and continue until the job is done or a person needs to step in.
Agentic AI development is the practice of designing these systems safely, with clear goals, limited permissions, reliable tools and checks at every important step.

paragraphs.html: AI agent vs chatbot is a common question. A chatbot mainly answers questions in a conversation, usually from a fixed knowledge base. An agent can also take action: create a ticket, update an order, book an appointment, prepare a report or send a follow-up, often across several systems.

paragraphs.text: In short, chatbots talk and agents work. Many businesses start with a chatbot and later add agent capabilities as trust and needs grow.

sections.h2: What Can AI Agents Do for Business?
sections.intro: What can AI agents do for business? Here are the types of agents we build most often.

items.title: AI Customer Service Agent
items.text: An AI customer service agent answers customer questions, checks order or booking status in your systems, updates details, processes simple requests and hands complex cases to staff with a full summary. Customers get faster service, and your team handles fewer repetitive tickets.

items.title: AI Operations Agent
items.text: An AI operations agent handles internal tasks such as checking stock levels, preparing purchase suggestions, reconciling records, chasing pending approvals and producing daily status summaries for managers.

items.title: AI Research Agent
items.text: An AI research agent gathers information from approved sources, such as websites, documents and internal databases, compares it and produces structured summaries. Sales teams use research agents to prepare for meetings, and managers use them to track competitors or market changes.

items.title: Autonomous AI Agents for Back-Office Tasks
items.text: Autonomous AI agents can run on a schedule or react to events, for example processing new enquiries overnight or monitoring a shared inbox. We set firm limits on what they can do alone and what needs approval.

items.title: AI Agents With Tool Calling
items.html: AI agents with tool calling connect to your software through secure APIs. Each tool has a narrow, clearly defined job, such as "look up order by number" or "create draft invoice," which makes agents more predictable and easier to test.

items.title: MCP Server Development
items.text: MCP server development uses the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting AI models to tools and data. We build MCP servers that expose your systems to AI agents in a controlled, reusable way, so the same connections can serve several agents or AI assistants.

items.title: Multi-Agent Systems
items.text: Multi-agent systems split complex work between specialised agents, for example one agent that gathers information, another that drafts a response and a third that checks it against your rules. This often produces more reliable results than a single agent trying to do everything.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop AI Agents
items.text: Human-in-the-loop AI agents pause for approval before sensitive actions, such as sending money, emailing important clients or changing records. Staff review, edit or approve with one click, and the agent continues.

paragraphs.text: Are AI agents reliable? They can be, when they are designed carefully. Reliability comes from narrow goals, well-defined tools, clear instructions, testing against real examples and approval steps for high-risk actions. Agents given broad, vague goals with unlimited access are the ones that fail.

We test every agent against a set of real scenarios before launch, including unusual and tricky cases, and we keep measuring accuracy after it goes live. When an agent cannot complete a task confidently, it records what it tried, explains where it got stuck and passes the case to a named person, so nothing is left half-finished or hidden from your team.

AI agent security and permissions are built in from the start. Each agent receives only the access it needs, using separate credentials, read-only access where possible and spending or action limits. Every action is logged, so you can see what the agent did and why. Sensitive data can stay within your own systems, and we choose AI providers with clear data-handling policies.

AI agent monitoring tracks every run, tool call, error and outcome. Dashboards show how many tasks agents complete, how often they ask for help and where they struggle. Alerts notify our team and yours if something goes wrong, and we use monitoring data to improve instructions and tools each month.

sections.h2: What to Look For in an AI Agent Development Company
sections.intro: Choosing an AI agent development company is different from buying an off-the-shelf tool. Before you sign, ask a few practical questions:

items.html: Do they test against real scenarios? Ask how accuracy is measured before and after launch.
How are permissions handled? Agents should never receive more access than their task needs.
Who owns the code and prompts? You should be able to keep, move or extend what is built.
What happens when the agent is unsure? Good agents hand over to people instead of guessing.
Is monitoring included? Agents need ongoing review, not a one-time delivery.

outro.text: A reliable development partner will answer these clearly and in writing. We include all five in every proposal, so you know exactly how your agent will behave, who can change it and how it will be supported after launch.

sections.h2: Our AI Agent Development Process and Timeline

items.title: Discovery (3 to 5 days)
items.text: We define the task, success measures, systems and risks.

items.title: Design (3 to 7 days)
items.text: We plan tools, permissions, approval steps and test scenarios.

items.title: Build (2 to 5 weeks)
items.text: We build the agent, tools and integrations in a safe test environment.

items.title: Testing (1 to 2 weeks)
items.text: We run real scenarios, measure accuracy and refine instructions.

items.title: Pilot launch (1 to 2 weeks)
items.text: The agent runs with close human review on live work.

items.title: Full launch and monitoring (ongoing)
items.text: We widen its scope gradually and report monthly.

paragraphs.text: A single focused agent is typically ready in 4 to 6 weeks. Multi-agent systems connected to several business tools usually take 8 to 10 weeks.

sections.h2: How Much Does an AI Agent Cost?

paragraphs.text: How much does an AI agent cost? It depends on the number of tools and systems involved, the complexity of decisions, approval steps and expected usage. Costs include a one-time design and build fee, AI model usage charges that grow with volume, hosting, and optional monthly monitoring and improvement.
We provide a clear estimate after discovery, along with expected time savings, so you can compare the investment with the value it should deliver.
Ask us for an AI agent case study relevant to your industry or use case. We share project details only with client approval, and we are happy to demonstrate example agents on a call.

items.q: Which AI models do you use?
items.a: We work with leading commercial models and open-source options, choosing based on accuracy, cost, speed, language needs and data requirements for each project.

items.q: Can an agent work in Malayalam or Arabic?
items.a: Yes. Modern models handle Malayalam, Arabic, Hindi and English well. We test each language with real examples before launch.

items.q: Will the agent make decisions without us?
items.a: Only the ones you allow. You decide which actions are automatic and which need approval, and you can change those limits at any time.
